correctness.rationale: The strongest singularity claim, on the explicitly scheme-theoretic reading in RESULT.md lines 6 and 35, is false for the usual Jacobian/Fitting singular subscheme. Over a splitting field the adjoint matrix is equivalent to rows v^T,(Sv)^T, S=diag(C,C^T), so its ideal is generated by cross-block quadratic products of eigenplane variables. Since dim X_f=4, Fitt_4(Ω_X) is generated by minors of size (2m+2)−4=2m−2 of the Jacobian of those quadrics. Its entries lie in the center ideal J=(v_{i,a}), and hence Fitt_4(Ω_X) is contained in J^(2m−2), a proper subideal of J for all m>=2 because J has nonzero degree-one part. In particular m=2 already contradicts equality of the usual singular subscheme with the reduced center. The proven statement is that its underlying non-smooth locus, or its reduced support, is the center. The other claims check: the Pfaffian matrix is alternating even in characteristic two; the cross-block ideal is the intersection of the coordinate-block primes, giving the reduced union and Hilbert series. Frobenius fixes a noncentral rational vector's unique eigenvalue, and each fixed two-plane has q^(2r)−1 nonzero vectors. Summing over factor degrees in the logarithm gives the asserted product; Möbius inversion recovers the degrees. The rank enumerator and commuting probability follow from the center translates and centralizer size q^(2m+2−rank). Analytical replay: RESULT.md §§1–7, with the Jacobian countercheck above. Frozen support inspected, not executed; no finite computation is necessary to certify the structural or arithmetic claims.

evidence: For A=diag(C,C^T), each prior eigenspace component is a two-plane with eigenvalue uniquely identifiable at a nonzero point. Frobenius permutes its eigenplanes as roots of f. Thus above each degree-d root orbit the noncentral piece contributes d(q^(2r)−1)q^(2r) points for d|r and zero otherwise. This yields the frozen Euler product by geometric-series logarithms; recovering orbit degrees is divisor Möbius inversion. The Hilbert series is that of monomials confined to one block times a polynomial ring; smoothness off the common center follows from the known component decomposition. The rank/commuting formulas just weigh each rank by q^-rank.

originality.rationale: The strongest primary match is Abo–Eklund–Kahle–Peterson (2016). Its ideal is exactly the adjoint-minor ideal after the frozen change of columns, before adjoining the center variables. Its diagonalizable case gives the claimed reduced union by specializing the eigenspace dimensions to two. That earlier theorem does not state this Lie-algebra zeta product, but the product and degree recovery are a mechanical consequence of the Frobenius permutation of these same linear components, whose eigenvalue labels are the roots of the input companion polynomial. Neither the covered geometric theorem nor that arithmetic specialization establishes a distinct substantive surviving result. The indexed six-dimensional bracket census is related separately, not credited as exact coverage of this scheme.

The comparison does not establish historical priority for writing this particular zeta formula. Gerstenhaber, On dominance and varieties of commuting matrices, JSTOR 1970379, did not yield decisive full text; this was not used as negative evidence.

value.rationale: The adjoint-rank scheme and its zeta function are natural invariants, and the contrast between base-field rank counts and factor-degree recovery is a useful interpretation. But this record's valid remainder is the standard diagonalizable eigenscheme specialized to doubled companion eigenspaces, and its finite-field formulas are determined directly by that known arrangement and the input factorization. There is no independent exact invariant demonstrated beyond those mechanical consequences, and the purported equality of singular schemes is false. A mere change to reduced singular support and credit to eigenscheme theory would not leave a substantive repaired finding.
